notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.8: "LINAGE-COUNTER must be qualified each time it is referenced if more than one file description entry containing a LINAGE clause has been specified in the source program." LinageFileOf is the one resolver of the register: a qualified reference takes the named file if its file description entry has a LINAGE clause (COBOL0863 otherwise), and an unqualified one resolves only when exactly one file with a LINAGE clause is in VisibleFiles, else COBOL5997. It has no edition arm, and VisibleFiles is the program's own files plus every containing program's GLOBAL files, which is the count of §2023:8.4.2.2.3 SR8 ("may be referenced within the source element in which the reference to LINAGE-COUNTER occurs"), not the 1985 one. For a program that contains no other and is contained in none the two counts are the same and the rule is met; probed at --std 85: two LINAGE files refuse each unqualified reference (DISPLAY, IF) and accept OF and IN with either file-name in DISPLAY, MOVE, ADD and a relation; one LINAGE file beside a file without LINAGE needs no qualifier; a qualifier naming a file without LINAGE is refused. The counts differ in a contained program that specifies one LINAGE file of its own under a containing program whose LINAGE file is GLOBAL: one file description entry with a LINAGE clause "has been specified in the source program" that holds the reference, so 1985 requires no qualifier, and the reference is to that program's own register (§1985:X.1.3.8: a program's reference is "to the object which that program describes rather than to the object, possessing the same name, described in another program"; §1985:X.1.3.8.2 uses "declared in a source program" for a program's own declarations, apart from those of a program it contains), while the compiler refuses it with COBOL5997 because the containing program's register is a global name (§1985:X.4.2.4 GR1) and so a second visible file. This reads "the source program" as the program that holds the reference; GnuCOBOL 3.2 at -std=cobol85 counts the same way and accepts the program (a regression net, not authority). Under the other reading, in which a contained program's file description entries count for the program that contains it, the compiler departs the other way: a containing program with one LINAGE file and a contained program with another, neither GLOBAL, compiles with an unqualified reference in each (probed). The witness is one program with two LINAGE files and DISPLAY LINAGE-COUNTER, refused with COBOL5997. No kb/Work note owns the fix.

next.reason: 1985: "if more than one file description entry containing a LINAGE clause has been specified in the source program"; 2023: "if more than one file description entry containing a LINAGE clause may be referenced within the source element in which the reference". 1985 counts every LINAGE file description in the source program. 2023 counts only those referenceable from the source element, so unqualified references in nested programs may now be allowed.
